title: GCD Class S_d(n)
content: The GCD class $S_d(n) = \{k \in \{0,\ldots,n-1\} : \gcd(k,n) = d\}$ partitions the integers modulo n by their greatest common divisor with n. Implemented as (range n).filter (fun k => Nat.gcd k n = d). The class S₁(n) is exactly the coprime residues mod n — the group (ℤ/nℤ)× — with |S₁| = φ(n) elements. Classes for different divisors are automatically disjoint since each k has a unique gcd with n.
mathContext: $S_d(n) = \{k \in \{0,\ldots,n-1\} : \gcd(k,n) = d\}$. Non-empty iff $d \mid n$. The class $S_1(n) = (\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^\times$ with $|S_1| = \varphi(n)$.

title: GCD Class Partition of {0,...,n-1}
content: Proves {0,...,n-1} = ⊔_{d|n} S_d(n): every k < n belongs to exactly one GCD class S_{gcd(k,n)}, and classes for different divisors are disjoint. Coverage is immediate: gcd(k,n) always divides n, so k ∈ S_{gcd(k,n)}. Disjointness follows from uniqueness of GCD. The Lean proof uses Finset.biUnion with a disjointness hypothesis verified by Finset.disjoint_filter.
mathContext: $\{0,\ldots,n-1\} = \bigsqcup_{d \mid n} S_d(n)$. For each $k$: $k \in S_{\gcd(k,n)}$ (coverage). If $d_1 \neq d_2$: $S_{d_1} \cap S_{d_2} = \emptyset$ (uniqueness of GCD).

title: Key Bijection: |S_d(n)| = φ(n/d)
content: The heart of the proof. The map k ↦ k/d bijects S_d(n) with the coprime set {m < n/d : gcd(m, n/d) = 1}. For k ∈ S_d: d divides k (since gcd(k,n) = d), so k/d is well-defined, and gcd(k/d, n/d) = gcd(k,n)/d = 1 (coprimality after cancellation). Injectivity: k₁/d = k₂/d with d|k₁, d|k₂ gives k₁ = k₂ by Nat.div_mul_cancel. Surjectivity: for coprime m < n/d, the element d·m ∈ S_d since gcd(d·m, d·(n/d)) = d·gcd(m,n/d) = d·1 = d. The Lean proof uses Finset.card_bij.
mathContext: Bijection $k \mapsto k/d : S_d(n) \xrightarrow{\sim} \{m < n/d : \gcd(m, n/d) = 1\}$. Uses $\gcd(k/d, n/d) = \gcd(k,n)/d = 1$ and inverse $m \mapsto d \cdot m$ with $\gcd(dm, dq) = d \cdot \gcd(m,q) = d$.

title: The Divisor Sum Identity n = Σ_{d|n} φ(n/d)
content: The main result: n = Σ_{d|n} φ(n/d), proved by summing the partition cardinalities. The chain: n = |{0,...,n-1}| = Σ_{d|n} |S_d(n)| = Σ_{d|n} φ(n/d), using card_range, card_biUnion (with disjointness), and card_gcdClass_eq_totient. Also proves the standard form Σ_{d|n} φ(d) = n via the divisor-symmetry reindexing d ↔ n/d, cross-validated against Mathlib's Nat.sum_totient.
mathContext: $n = \sum_{d \mid n} \varphi(n/d) = \sum_{d \mid n} \varphi(d)$. The reindexing $d \leftrightarrow n/d$ uses the involution on the divisor set: $\{d : d \mid n\} \cong \{d : d \mid n\}$ via $d \mapsto n/d$.

title: Partition of Unity and Probabilistic Interpretation
content: Proves Σ_{d|n} φ(n/d)/n = 1 over ℚ by dividing the integer identity by n. The probabilistic content: if U is uniform on {0,...,n-1}, then P(gcd(U,n) = d) = φ(n/d)/n. The divisors of n with weights φ(n/d)/n form a probability mass function on the divisor lattice. This connects to the Haar measure on ℤ/nℤ and to the distribution theory of GCD random variables, which appears in the analysis of random number generators and cryptographic protocols.
mathContext: $\sum_{d \mid n} \frac{\varphi(n/d)}{n} = 1$. Probabilistic: $P(\gcd(U,n) = d) = \varphi(n/d)/n$ where $U \sim \text{Uniform}(\{0,\ldots,n-1\})$. For $d=1$: $P(\gcd(U,n)=1) = \varphi(n)/n$ — the 'probability of coprimality.'

title: Concrete Verifications for n = 6, 7, 12, 30
content: Uses native_decide to verify the identity for specific values. For n=6: divisors {1,2,3,6}, GCD classes S₁={1,5}, S₂={2,4}, S₃={3}, S₆={0}, sizes 2,2,1,1 matching φ(6)=2, φ(3)=2, φ(2)=1, φ(1)=1. For prime p=7: S₁={1,2,3,4,5,6} (size 6=φ(7)), S₇={0} (size 1=φ(1)), sum=7. These serve as sanity checks and illustrate the GCD partition structure concretely.
